articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a whopping 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw that was already public. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day of the year because apparently browsers are just fancy attack surfaces now.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: CISA confirms active exploitation of a critical cPanel vulnerability affecting millions of websites. At least one victim already got hit with ransomware because nothing says 'welcome to the internet' like getting pwned through your hosting panel.

articles.title: Week in review: High-severity LPE vulnerability in the Linux kernel, cPanel 0-day exploited for months
articles.summary: CISA adds CVE-2026-31431 to their Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list - a Linux root access bug that's being actively exploited. Because what's a Friday without another reminder that everything is broken?

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence hacked old routers to mass-harvest Microsoft Office authentication tokens. Classic state-sponsored efficiency: why develop new exploits when you can just abuse the garbage firmware everyone forgot to patch?

articles.title: ADT data breach exposes customer information
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Trellix got breached and had source code stolen from their repository. Nothing quite says 'trust us with your security' like getting your own code yoinked by threat actors.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's anti-VPN law goes into effect, because nothing says 'freedom' like making privacy tools illegal. Predictably, VPN usage is surging as residents scramble to maintain basic digital rights.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: Public records requests exposed massive ALPR surveillance networks, so naturally states want to block what the public can see. Because transparency is only good until it reveals how dystopian the surveillance state has become.

articles.title: Getting Digital Fairness Right: EFF's Recommendations for the EU's Digital Fairness Act
articles.summary: Germany doxes 'UNKN,' the elusive leader of REvil and GandCrab ransomware gangs - turns out he's 31-year-old Russian Daniil Shchukin. Finally putting a face to the chaos behind 130+ acts of digital mayhem.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after those epic 2022 SMS phishing campaigns. Another one bites the dust in the endless game of cybercrime whack-a-mole.

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: UK's cyber agency warns that AI-powered bug hunting is about to unleash decades of buried technical debt all at once. Get ready for the mother of all patch tsunamis as AI excavates every shortcut developers thought they'd buried forever.
